data.title: Hedge funds show mixed positioning in CoreWeave; Soros and Tepper add, D1 Capital exits
data.description:
Hedge fund activity in CoreWeave (CRWV) remained mixed in the third quarter, with prominent investors George Soros and David Tepper increasing their exposure, while Brad Gerstner's Altimeter Capital trimmed its position and D1 Capital Partners exited entirely.

According to the latest reported holdings:

  • Soros Fund Management (George Soros) more than doubled its stake, increasing its holdings to 612,000 shares from 300,000, a 104% increase.
  • Appaloosa Management (David Tepper) raised its position to 1.22 million shares from 1.08 million, an increase of ~13%.
  • Altimeter Capital (Brad Gerstner) reduced its holdings to 4.78 million shares from 6.07 million, cutting its position by about 21%.
  • D1 Capital Partners exited its entire CoreWeave (CRWV) position, selling its previously reported 628,000 shares.
  • Nvidia (NVDA) maintained its substantial strategic holding of 47.21 million CoreWeave shares, unchanged from its previous reported position.

The latest positioning highlights diverging views among institutional investors. While Soros and Tepper appear to be building exposure to the AI infrastructure company, Altimeter's reduction and D1 Capital's exit indicate a more cautious stance among some investors. The stock is down 37% YTD.

Of note, CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS) were among the leading decliners in neocloud computing stocks on Monday, as investors continued to flee artificial intelligence-linked companies and the sector dealt with the fallout from Nvidia's (NVDA) scandal.

data.title: Enel expands U.S. renewables portfolio with 317 MW solar deal
data.description:
Enel (ENLAY) said Friday it agreed to acquire a portfolio of solar plants in the U.S. from clean energy infrastructure developer energyRe, boosting its installed renewable capacity in North America to 13.5 GW, including storage assets.

Enel (ENLAY) said the plants, located in South Carolina, have a total installed capacity of 317 MW and an expected average annual electricity production exceeding 540 GWh.

Financial terms were not disclosed, but Enel (ENLAY) said it expects the deal to increase its net financial debt by ~$255M once ​the plants ​are completed ⁠and considering the effects of their entry into service.

The company estimates the assets ​will ⁠generate an additional $30M in annual EBITDA after they become operational.

The deal is part of the strategy outlined at Enel's (ENLAY) Capital Markets Day in February, which identified acquisitions of existing renewable assets in established markets as a way to expand generation capacity.

data.title: Stocks jump more than 10% six months after the VIX reaches 28-33
data.description:
When the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) closes around the 30 level, U.S. stocks tend to increase more than 10% in the following six months.

The VIX ended above 28 on Thursday, and it’s currently above 30, having increased more than 70% in the past month.

“Readings between 28 and 33 have historically proven a strong buying opportunity, with average six-month forward returns nearly +10%,” analysts at Finom Group noted.

The forward six-month S&P 500 (SP500) return when the volatility index (VIX) is between 28.7 and 33.5 is currently implied to be 9.3%. When the VIX is above 33.5, S&P 500 (SP500) returns jump to 12.7% in the next six months.

 

 

 

“This is likely ‘peaking’ volatility, bottoming equity regime,” they said.

The S&P 500 (SP500) opened below the red line, currently at $7.144.41, down 0.4% in early morning trade. It has declined almost 3% in the past six months.

data.title: U.S. stock market moves lower as Anthropic drops post IPO
data.description:
U.S. stocks tumbled on Friday, extending a broad market selloff that has pushed the major indices toward their steepest weekly losses in more than a year, as renewed weakness in artificial intelligence stocks added to concerns across Wall Street.

Sentiment toward artificial intelligence stocks remained under pressure after Anthropic's (ANT) much-anticipated public market debut failed to provide the boost investors had hoped for, extending a volatile week for equities.

S&P 500 (SP500) -0.%, the Dow (DJI) -0.9%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) -1.3%.

The latest declines followed a bruising Thursday session in which all three major indexes fell more than 2%, with the Dow closing below 50,000 for the first time since June. AI-related stocks remained under pressure, with Anthropic extending losses after its public market debut and dragging chipmakers including Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Nvidia (NVDA) and Micron (MU) lower. 

The Dow is on track for its worst weekly performance since April 2025, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are headed for their steepest weekly declines in more than a year.

Meanwhile, BJ’s Wholesale Club (BJ) beat expectations on nearly every metric in the third quarter, as higher membership fee income, increased traffic, and digitally enabled sales pushed revenue and earnings per share above Wall Street forecasts.

data.title: Elastic's guide appears conservative as analysts highlight cloud growth
data.description:
Elastic (ESTC) reported its second-quarter fiscal 2027 results post-market on Thursday, and although third-quarter guidance came in less than expected, due in part to foreign exchange headwinds, analysts were positive.

Shares were down 2% during early Friday morning market action.

RBC Capital Markets maintained its Outperform rating following the results but reduced its price target to $105 from $125.

"Elastic reported another strong quarter with all guided metrics ahead of expectations and acceleration in both sales-led subscription and Elastic Cloud revenue," said RBC analyst Matthew Hedberg in an investor note.

"Sales-led subscription growth accelerated to +19% growth vs. +17% q/q and Elastic Cloud revenue growth accelerated to +23% vs. 20% q/q," he added. "Consumption outperformance was the driver of the quarter, and while it was broad-based, Americas and global public sector were strongest, with security and search outpacing overall company growth. We do not believe strength in the quarter was a result of any deal pull-ins."

Meanwhile, Morgan Stanley retained it Equal-weight rating but nudged its price target up to $85 from $75.

"For FY27, total revenue/sales-led subscription guidance was raised on a cc basis to +15.9%/+18.0% from +15.3%/ +17.5% prior but was generally unchanged on a reported dollar basis despite the ~2% beat in 2Q27," said Morgan Stanley analyst Sanjit Singh in a Friday investor report. "For 3Q27, both revenue and sales-led subscription missed consensus by ~2%."

"This reflects 2 factors: 1) FX as the dollar strengthened against Euro and UK pound and 2) prudent conservatism given geopolitical volatility in Europe and the Middle East," he added. "Furthermore, the trajectory of sales-led subscription growth is expected to be weighted more towards 4Q27, as management now projects 3Q27 cc sales-led subscription growth of +16% and 4Q27 cc sales-led subscription growth of +19%."

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway cut to Hold from Buy at Argus Research on valuation
data.description:
Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) was downgraded to Hold from Buy at Argus Research as the shares surpassed the investment bank's target of $550.

Shares were 0.12% lower at $571.34 before the market open on Friday.

"Recently, the shares have risen on significant share repurchases and as an 'anti-AI' trade. Wecontinue to think the shares remain suitable as a long-term core Financial sector holding in a diversified portfolio," said the research note.

"On valuation, the stock is trading at 25-times our 2027 operating EPS forecast. We believe the shares are fully valued at current levels and a HOLD rating is now appropriate," said the note.

BRK.B is rated Buy by the Wall Street analysts as well as Seeking Alpha authors. Quant sees the stock as Hold.

data.title: FICO expands partnership with Xactus, broadening FICO Preferred's reach
data.description:
Fair Isaac (FICO) expanded its partnership with verification systems provider Xactus, bringing FICO's new pricing options to Xactus lender and broker clients and to mortgage resellers, the company said Friday.

Xactus will make the FICO Preferred Program available to all mortgage industry clients and will extend access to mortgage credit reseller clients served by the XedaLink and SharperLending platforms.

Through the monthly FICO Preferred Program, participating lenders can access the Classic FICO Score and FICO Score 10T for a $10 wholesale price per bureau, per borrower, for the bundled scores (FICO wholesale price unchanged for 2027). The Classic FICO Score has been the mortgage industry standard for almost three decades. FICO Score 10T, using recent data, integrates trended credit data, supporting more predictive consumer credit risk management.

Fair Isaac (FICO) stock ticked up 0.1% in premarket trading.

data.title: Keysight: Analysts highlight strong orders, upbeat outlook
data.description:
Keysight (KEYS) reported stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings and revenue, with analysts pointing to robust demand for artificial intelligence-related testing equipment and strength across its broader business.

The company reported fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of $3.61 per share, beating the analyst consensus estimate of $3.38. Revenue rose 40.1% from a year earlier to $1.99B, exceeding expectations of $1.95B. 

Keysight forecasts first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $2.04B to $2.06B, above the analyst consensus of $1.98B. It expects adjusted earnings of $3.63 to $3.69 per share, compared with estimates of $3.25.

"KEYS remains a Swiss-army knife way to play AI, with portfolio breadth supporting a 20%+ FY27 growth outlook. Strong orders underpin our OW view, though backlog conversion is taking longer. Raising estimates but lowering PT to $400 as we roll to FY28 given AI valuation pullback," according to Morgan Stanley analysts. Morgan Stanley lowered its price target to $400 from $425, citing a broader pullback in valuations across AI-related companies.

The brokerage highlighted 49% year-over-year growth in core orders and a book-to-bill ratio of 1.17, indicating orders are outpacing sales. It said Keysight offers broad exposure to AI spending, spanning chip designers, networking and interconnect suppliers, manufacturers, and data center operators.

Keysight's AI-related bookings increased 2.5 times in fiscal 2026, while its AI customer base nearly doubled, Morgan Stanley said. 

Bank of America also reiterated its Buy rating, pointing to strong order growth and demand across several markets.

Keysight's core orders rose 49% year over year to $2.34B in the fourth quarter, beating Bank of America's estimate of $2.13B and the consensus estimate of $2.17B.

The brokerage said there were no clear signs of an order peak, noting that demand was also growing in semiconductors, general electronics, automotive, and energy. Orders in aerospace, defense, and government also grew at a double-digit rate across the Americas, Europe, and Asia.

Bank of America raised its fiscal 2027 adjusted earnings estimate by $1.45 to $15.02 per share, representing 32% annual growth. It expects core revenue to increase 22% in the year.

The brokerage also pointed to the potential for a new growth driver from the development of 6G wireless technology, with orders expected to begin gaining traction in the second half of fiscal 2027. But Bank of America lowered its price objective to $375 from $405.

data.title: Tweedy, Browne initiate multiple new positions and exit several holdings in Q3 2026
data.description:
• All four Tweedy, Browne funds posted positive returns in Q3 2026, with three outperforming their respective benchmarks. International Value Fund (TBGVX) and International Value Fund II–Currency Unhedged (TBCUX) gained 2.09% and 2.75%, respectively, versus a 0.81% advance for MSCI EAFE. Buybacks. Dividends + Value Fund (TBHDX) advanced 3.37%, outperforming MSCI World's 1.88% gain and MSCI World High Dividend Yield Index's 1.07% return. Value Fund (TWEBX) rose 1.29%, trailing MSCI World's 1.88% gain.

  • The funds initiated new positions in Aptiv (NYSE: APTV), LVMH Moët Hennessy (LVMUY), Minth Group (MNTHF), Puregold Price Club (PGCMF), and Toyota Motor (NYSE: TM).

  • Separately, buybacks. Dividends + Value Fund initiated positions in Albertsons (NYSE: ACI), PT Astra International (PTAIY), Bangkok Life Assurance, Hikma Pharmaceuticals (HKMPY), Jumbo (JUMSF), Springer Nature (SPGDF), and Toyo Tire (TOTTF).

  • In Q3 2026, funds fully exited Teleperformance (TLPFY), Transcosmos (TRCLF), Alliance Global Group (ALGGY), Kuraray (KURRY), Adris Grupa, and LX Holdings.

  • Separately, buybacks. Dividends + Value Fund fully exited Haitian International (HAIIF), Hang Lung Group (HNLGY), LG Corp., Metropolitan Bank & Trust, Truist Financial (TFC), Uni-President China (UPCHY), and Western Union (NYSE: WU).

  • Outlook: Management expects elevated valuations, higher interest rates, and uncertain returns on AI investments to reinforce the importance of price-sensitive investing. The funds remain focused on undervalued businesses with strong balance sheets, durable competitive advantages, and meaningful free cash flow.

data.title: Klarna trades lower as Polish rival said to plan IPO
data.description:
Klarna Group (KLAR) was trading lower amid media reports of its Polish rival PayPo's potential initial public offering in Warsaw.

KLAR was down 2.13% to $12.40 during pre-market trading on Friday.

Buy-now-pay-later services provider, PayPo, is working with Citigroup (C) and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) on an IPO that could take place as soon as next year, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg News.

The IPO could raise several hundred million dollars and provide a partial exit for the fintech's investors, according to the sources, who asked not to be identified discussing confidential information.

Separately, Klarna has partnered with Adyen (ADYYF) (ADYEY) to enable the latter's merchants to pay with Klarna when an AI agent checks out for them.
